title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Main Building No. 1
geometryBasis: The named 56-point Main Building No. 1 outline and six separate native upper tower part polygons give the footprint and detailed setbacks. Use the architect’s 243.4 m final elevation and the mapped 133/176/207 m subdivisions as the primary exterior sections.
sectionBasis: The plaza-side sample from Japan’s official DEM5A controls site contact. The frozen global terrain serves as a documented comparison. The architect reports 243.4 m, and Tokyo’s authority identifies 48 levels and the floor-45 public observatories. Window dimensions, stone relief, crown mechanical details and vertical relationships within the entrance block are reconstructed.
limitations: Includes standing Main Building No. 1 and its entrance facades. The separately mapped No. 2, assembly, station, sculpture, artwork and raised public footbridges remain outside model geometry.
Native footprint, setbacks and documented 243.4 m rise determine scale. Window bay spacing, exact granite patterns, pilotis, rooftop mechanical fixtures and lighting details are reconstructed.

The site grade and foundation use Japan’s official DEM5A. The frozen global DEM independently shows rooftop and urban artifacts. Runtime snaps to its ordinary terrain provider. Plaza and entrance grades remain approximate.
